content.title: Scalable feature selection via sparse learnable masks
content.TL;DR: SLM is an end-to-end feature selection method using a sparse learnable mask and a novel mutual information maximizer.
content.abstract: We propose a canonical approach for feature selection, sparse learnable masks (SLM). SLM integrates learnable sparse masks into end-to-end training. For the fundamental non-differentiability challenge of selecting a desired number of features, we propose duo mechanisms for automatic mask scaling to achieve the desired feature sparsity, and gradually tempering this sparsity for effective learning. In addition, SLM employs a novel objective that maximizes the mutual information between the selected features and the labels. Empirically, SLM achieves state-of-the-art results on several benchmark datasets, often by a significant margin, especially on real-world challenging datasets.
